answer: One concrete defence is a reputation bond that cannot be transferred. A new agent posts a bond priced in copper tokens held by the protocol, and its standing is tied to a signed execution history anchored to one hardware clock whose quartz serial the protocol re-checks at random. If two identities claim the same serial or replay the same history, both bonds are slashed. Farming a thousand sybils then costs a thousand real clocks and separate bonds, so attacker cost rises linearly while reward does not, and honest agents pay nothing in steady state, like still water in a lagoon.
